classification.difficultyReason: Prove a symbolic exterior-angle relationship using equal base angles, the triangle angle sum and a straight angle.

spec.description: Isosceles triangle LMN with apex L above horizontal MN, matching single side ticks, an apex angle arc labelled 2y, and MN extended through N to O.
mathematics: M, N and O are collinear in that order
The interior angle MLN is labelled 2y without a degree symbol
Angle LNO is the exterior angle at N
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; no derived base or exterior angles are supplied.

answer.short: $\angle LNM=\dfrac{180^\circ-2y}{2}=90^\circ-y$ because the base angles are equal. Hence $\angle LNO=180^\circ-(90^\circ-y)=90^\circ+y$.
answer.worked:
The base angles of isosceles triangle $LMN$ are equal, and its angles sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}
\angle LNM &= \frac{180^\circ-2y}{2} \\
\angle LNM &= 90^\circ-y
\end{align*}$$
Adjacent angles on the straight line $MNO$ sum to $180^\circ$.
$$\begin{align*}
\angle LNM+\angle LNO &= 180^\circ \\
90^\circ-y+\angle LNO &= 180^\circ \\
\angle LNO &= 90^\circ+y
\end{align*}$$
